graphEvents.label: Explicit LAN Tailscale and custom modes
MobileCLI auth protocol and setup sources

label: Pairing generates a random 32-byte token, stores only a domain-separated SHA-256 verifier server-side, and places the raw token in the one-time pairing result.
Auth proof is HMAC-SHA256 over a transcript containing server ID, credential ID, client/server nonces, and mobile installation ID; response fields must match before proof validation.
Credential scopes map to operation families and are checked together with on-disk credential activity, so revocation affects already-authenticated clients at later operations.
Rotation revokes all existing credentials before issuing a new QR credential; individual revocation is persistent and successful auth records last_used_at.
The QR is device-level, encoding authority, device metadata, auth version, server ID, credential ID, token, and secure-scheme flag before session discovery.
Setup has explicit Local, Tailscale, and Custom modes with local-IP detection, Tailscale status/IP detection, or explicit WebSocket URL input.
The browser must keep the pairing secret separate from server metadata and must treat auth failure, capability denial, and transport failure as different states.
A paired device record should identify a daemon and discover sessions after authentication; it should not treat the QR as a session identity.
The server sources define auth and network-mode semantics but do not define browser secret storage, mixed-content handling, or capability downgrade messages.
The QR includes a one-time token even though the persisted server credential contains only a derived verifier.

direction: Infer browser storage and connectivity policy directly from the desktop implementation
reason: The sources specify server persistence and CLI setup behavior, but not browser security boundaries or web reachability constraints.
